long_biography.plain_text:
Cabinet government in Italy operates through collective deliberation. The Council of Ministers sets the government's overall direction, while the President of the Council coordinates ministers and maintains unity across their work. Presidency departments supply legal, administrative and technical support for decisions, regulation and relations with Parliament and European institutions.

This machinery survives elections, resignations and changes of cabinet. Ministries and other public bodies carry out policy within their assigned responsibilities; defence includes the Italian Navy as the state's maritime operational component. Assets held by those bodies remain public or custodial resources. They do not belong personally to the president of the Council, a minister, naval officer or civil servant.

uncertainties.detail: Italy Government is a broad database label rather than the official title of one legal person, ministry or department. Official sources define the Government of the Republic, while vessel reporting identifies the Italian Navy and its High Tyrrhenian Command as the narrower public custodian. The dossier preserves the broad institution rather than silently renaming it as the Navy.

Two independent 2014 reports say Sanjir was confiscated and assigned to the Italian Navy. One describes the assignment as after confiscation, while other contemporary coverage noted continuing procedural objections. No reviewed official judgment, registry extract or later disposal record independently confirms the final present-day title chain.

The authoritative input marks the government relationship current from January 2014. Public reporting establishes state seizure or confiscation and Navy assignment at that time but does not verify 2026 registration, current physical custody, operational condition or whether the asset was later returned, sold, transferred or decommissioned.

Some contemporary reports described a planned presidential role, but La Nazione quoted the Italian Navy as saying no Navy vessel had been assigned or proposed to the Head of State. The dossier therefore makes no presidential-yacht claim and does not associate Sanjir with any individual president.

Forbes contains editorial references to the Italian government and profiles of individual Italian officeholders, but no dedicated institutional profile was found. No person page can represent this government record, so no Forbes social is proposed.
